correctness.rationale: The exact gap polynomial follows from parity-restricted switch selections on disjoint cyclic paths. The attainable switch totals form a contiguous interval on even integers; independently extremizing its lower and upper endpoints proves the necessary and sufficient size threshold for every support. All edge/singleton/boundary cases were reconstructed and the homotopy, hypothesis-count, and blockwise adaptive arguments checked. Every support through n=11 and every trace of size at most three was tested directly. A separate full depth-four tree verifies the n=5 first adaptive gap. Finite tests are corroborative, not a substitute for the general proof.

evidence: The original linear theorem excludes the simultaneous two endpoints, which become adjacent after cycle closure. Its lower completion interval relies on an external free edge and cannot itself certify the closing-edge parity case.

Johnson studies the VC complexity of translates of a given word and infinite binary strings, so his assertion does not quantify over all words with exactly k cyclic switches or specify their support traces.
Ghazi et al. address composition/closure of concept families, not an exact finite shattering polynomial or cyclic change-point multiplicities.
In the two-block circular partition result the query domain is unordered vertex pairs; one-bit vertex queries can distinguish global block complementation while pair queries cannot.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: None of these available statements directly implies the entire new conclusion (all-parameter uniform support classification, coefficient-exact completions and first finite vertex-query adaptive gap). Standard circular-arc VC facts cover the sparse-regime dimension scale, so those facts are explicitly excluded from any assertion of methodological novelty.

evidence: The public linear exact-switch theorem has a nonshattered endpoint pair and rank min(k+1,n-k), rather than the present cyclic uniform rank min(k+1,n-k+1). Its full RESULT.md states that cyclic variants are outside scope.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A binary cyclic exact-switch family may be viewed as labeled cyclic alternating runs or a union of exactly k/2 positive circular arcs, but all switch edges remain mandatory, not merely bounded in number. Existing interval bounds and the path model give useful comparison, not an equivalent all-parameter theorem; the unqueried-gap parity minimax and exact trace polynomial must still be proved.

originality.rationale: A literature-led comparison identified the nearest linear exact-switch theorem, classical interval-union VC theory, general online closure bounds, the original binary-strings VC paper and a different pair-query circular-partition class. Each was compared by actual hypotheses and query predicates, not title. The exact feasible cyclic switching support structure and trace multiplicity product are not implied by the inspected theorems. Priority remains provisional in the presence of unindexed equivalent sign-change/circular-arc results.
residual_risks: The cyclic model can be described as exactly k/2 circular arcs of ones; earlier learning theory under that language may state part or all of the criterion.

Finite online dimensions beyond the n=5 first gap are checked computationally only and not claimed in closed form.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact-change-budget classifier family, not an arbitrary finite slice. Closing one boundary deletes a genuine endpoint-parallel matroid obstruction and simultaneously changes the high-switch rank cap. The theorem supplies every shattered support, exact full face polynomial, all-label trace multiplicities, uniform-matroid topology, and a logarithmically diverging adaptive advantage at fixed switch budget. Existing interval VC bounds do not furnish that complete classification or dense restriction. The topological statement uses known matroid consequences and is not claimed as an independent discovery.
